anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to process or return far more data than business logic actually requires.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Optimizer cost inputs are stale, incomplete, or misleading, causing systematic misestimation of cardinalities and sub-optimal plan choices.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The underlying storage layer is saturated, so physical read/write latency, IOPS, or bandwidth become the dominant bottleneck.

When all three conditions coexist, the database exhibits extreme and highly variable response times, runaway I/O wait percentages despite available CPU, repeated slow-query log entries for the same statements, frequent plan recompilations with wildly shifting row-estimate errors, prolonged lock holding, and application timeouts or cascading retries. Execution plans often show full or large index scans chosen on the basis of bad statistics, while the sheer volume of unnecessary data access generated by poorly written SQL floods the already saturated storage subsystem, driving queue depths and device wait times even higher. Batch windows stretch, checkpoint and log-flush operations compete with data reads, and both OLTP and analytical sessions experience head-of-line blocking on I/O.

Causally, inefficient SQL amplifies the impact of stale statistics: wide scans and non-selective predicates make the optimizer’s reliance on accurate cardinalities critical; when those statistics are outdated, it is more likely to choose plans that exacerbate data access. The resulting surge in physical I/O pushes the storage layer to or beyond its throughput limits, inflating latency. Elevated I/O latency in turn prolongs statement and transaction duration, delaying or suppressing automatic statistics refresh and leaving poor plans in place longer. The feedback loop between bad SQL, bad estimates, and saturated storage compounds resource contention, driving the database into a persistent degraded-performance state.

entry.official_definition: Read timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol read operation exceeds mysqlx_read_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network read operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
